description:
Redwood Inference is running a reliability program focused on SLO attainment, MTTR reduction, and graceful degradation across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This project (“Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping”) standardizes how incidents are classified (top incident types, contributing factors, impacted surfaces) and maps each category to (a) a primary owning team/service, (b) escalation paths, and (c) remediation SLAs (time-to-mitigate and time-to-permanent-fix targets by severity/tier).

Goals:
- Create a v1 incident taxonomy that is simple enough to use during active response, but structured enough for trend reporting and prioritization.
- Establish a single source of truth for “who owns what” (services and incident categories) to reduce paging ambiguity and handoff delays.
- Define remediation SLAs by incident category + severity (e.g., routing failures vs capacity exhaustion vs runtime crashes), including expectations for customer communications.
- Implement the taxonomy in operational tooling (incident bot/forms, postmortem templates, dashboards) and backfill/normalize recent incidents for baseline metrics.

Scope:
- Production incidents across Hosted API and Dedicated pools; Private incidents included where Redwood is the primary operator (day-2 ops). Security incidents remain governed by Security IR process but may share metadata fields.
- Updates to incident intake (Slack/incident bot), postmortem templates, SRE dashboards, and support escalation playbooks.
- Ownership mapping at two levels: service-level (e.g., smart-routing, scheduler, GPU fleet) and category-level (e.g., “capacity exhaustion” -> Infra/Fleet).

Out of scope (v1):
- Re-architecting services for reliability; this project feeds the follow-on reliability roadmap.
- Building a full incident management product; only incremental tooling changes.

Key stakeholders:
- SRE/Incident Command: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Miles Thornton, Aisha Bello
- Infra/Fleet/Networking: Irene Choi, Vanessa Ortiz, Keiko Yamamoto, Victor Alvarez
- Platform (routing/control plane/telemetry): Priya Natarajan, Mina Haddad, Ethan Park, Logan Wright
- Runtime (kernels/scheduling): Mateo Alvarez, Sofia Ivanova, Hiro Tanaka
- Observability: Allison Grant, Sergio Costa
- Support/CS escalation and comms: Dev Patel, Jasmine Liu, Rachel Kim
- Product alignment (SLAs/Console surfaces): Marissa Cole, Lauren Bishop, Paula Mendes
- Program management: Talia Benson

Timeline (typical 6–8 weeks):
1) Discovery (1–2 weeks): inventory last 2–3 quarters of incidents, cluster top failure modes, draft candidate taxonomy.
2) Taxonomy + ownership design (2 weeks): define categories, required metadata fields, and ownership mapping; review with Eng/SRE/Support.
3) Tooling + process rollout (2–3 weeks): implement fields in incident bot, update postmortem template, build dashboards, train on-call and support.
4) Backfill + baseline reporting (1 week): normalize recent incidents; publish baseline top categories and a monthly review cadence.

Deliverables:
- Confluence: published taxonomy + metadata standard, remediation SLA table, ownership map, and updated incident process docs.
- Linear: an initiative with implementation issues, dependencies, and rollout checklist.
- GitHub: PRs for incident-bot, slo-toolkit/observability-pack, and minimal console/dashboard wiring.
- Slack/Jira/Gmail: coordination threads, support escalation examples, and leadership sign-off on SLAs/customer comms.

Constraints:
- Must be fast to apply during an incident (low cognitive load, limited required fields).
- Must not conflict with existing severity definitions and SLO/error-budget reporting.
- Ownership mapping must match actual on-call rotations and paging routes to avoid “paper ownership.”

files.description: Primary spec for incident taxonomy v1: category definitions, required/optional fields, examples, and guidance for choosing categories during live incidents vs postmortems.
Standard for incident metadata fields (category, impacted surface, customer tier, region, contributing factors) including allowed values and how they map to metrics/dashboards.
ADR capturing the decision to adopt taxonomy v1, key trade-offs (simplicity vs granularity), and how ownership is assigned/maintained.
Table mapping (severity x incident category x tier) to remediation SLAs (TTM/TTR), escalation expectations, and follow-up requirements.
Process update: when and how to set category/owner during incident declaration, minimum required fields, and rules for reclassification after the fact.
Updated postmortem template section(s) enforcing taxonomy fields, owner assignment, and remediation SLA tracking for action items.
Runbook for incident-bot usage: new form fields, examples, troubleshooting missing fields, and how data lands in dashboards.
Analysis of recent incidents clustered into top types; includes baseline metrics (counts, customer impact, MTTR) to justify taxonomy priorities.
Spec for dashboards: incident volume by category, MTTR/TTM by owner team, error budget burn correlation, and monthly reporting views.
Support/CS playbook mapping incident categories to customer messaging guidance, expected ETAs, and when to page Eng/SRE.
Working doc with drafts, open questions, edge cases, and notes from stakeholder reviews before the Confluence version is finalized.
Spreadsheet of last 2–3 quarters incidents with manual labels, clustering columns, impacted components, and candidate taxonomy mapping.
Spreadsheet mapping services/modules to owning team, on-call rotation, escalation Slack channels, and SME backups.
Spike notes on how incident metadata will be ingested (Slack/incident bot -> datastore) and joined with metrics for dashboards.
Infra-specific notes defining capacity/fleet/network incident subtypes and the boundary between autoscaling issues vs routing issues.
Draft of customer-facing implications: how remediation SLAs relate to contract SLAs, and standard language for enterprise comms.
Initiative tracker: “Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping” with milestones, owners (SRE lead + platform lead), and rollout checklist.
Define taxonomy v1 categories and required fields; includes acceptance criteria and review plan with SRE/Platform/Runtime/Support.
Create ownership mapping for top incident categories (primary team + secondary/escalation) and align with on-call rotations.
Implement taxonomy fields in incident-bot (Slack modal/commands) and ensure fields are mandatory on declare/escalate.
Add validation + allowed-values enforcement for category fields; include migration strategy when taxonomy values change.
Backfill last 90 days of incidents with taxonomy categories; define sampling method and quality checks.
Dashboards: build incident volume/MTTR by category and owner; define data sources, refresh cadence, and alert thresholds.
Update postmortem template to include taxonomy fields + remediation SLA section; roll out to #postmortems and Confluence.
Update runbooks and IC checklist to require category + owner assignment within X minutes of incident declaration.
Define remediation SLA mapping (TTM/TTR) by category; coordinate with Product/CS for customer comm expectations.
Add monthly incident taxonomy review meeting + reporting deck automation (top categories, regressions, ownership changes).
PM alignment: ensure remediation SLAs and taxonomy don’t conflict with contractual SLA language; define what is customer-visible.
Console/rollouts requirement: add filters/grouping by incident category for internal ops views (if applicable).
Design task: lightweight UI mock for internal incident dashboard (category chips, owner grouping, drill-down).
PR: Add incident taxonomy fields to Slack incident declaration flow (modal fields, defaults, validation, unit tests).
PR: Ownership auto-suggestion based on selected category + impacted service; includes config file and fallback behavior.
PR: Extend SLO toolkit data model to ingest incident metadata and compute MTTR by category/owner.
PR: New dashboards/alerts for incident category trends; includes Grafana/metrics config and documentation.
PR: Emit standardized incident-related annotations from control plane (e.g., routing degraded mode events) to support category attribution.
Customer ticket: recurring 5xx/timeouts with unclear ownership; used as example motivating category-to-owner mapping and better escalation.
Customer ticket: dedicated capacity saturation incidents; includes logs/regions and maps to new “capacity exhaustion / autoscaling” taxonomy.
Customer ticket: streaming disconnects during peak; triage notes and eventual categorization as “edge/gateway streaming” vs runtime.
Internal support ticket: request to update incident intake form and ensure taxonomy fields are required for status updates.

Thread: Platform owners review category list and push for consistent mapping to services (routing, policy, control plane).

Thread: Support asks for category->playbook mapping and what fields they should expect during an active escalation.
Thread: IC checklist update proposal; discussion about making category mandatory at declaration time vs within 15 minutes.

Thread: Monthly review cadence proposal; who attends, what metrics are reported, and how ownership changes are approved.
